title: KEC - Management Credibility Score (T&D peer calibration, Nov 2026)
body: Promise tracker on KEC International (peer calibration for SKIPPER). 8 concalls (Feb-2025 to Nov-2026); 75 promises extracted, 58 scored. Status counts: {'delivered': 13, 'partly': 7, 'missed': 26, 'moved-goalpost': 9, 'pending': 15, 'unverifiable': 2, 'withdrawn': 3}. Weighted delivery ratio 19.8% (specificity-only 26.9%; raw hit rate 22.4%); MCS -0.601. Candour index 31.1%. FY25 promises were broadly met (order inflow 24,689 vs 25,000; net debt 4,558 in the 4,500-5,000 range) but FY26 was a near-total miss on the group numbers: revenue +7.6% vs 15% (stated four times), EBITDA ~7.1% vs 8-8.5% (and +150 bp), net debt 6,722 vs 4,500, interest 2.8% vs 2.5%, NWC ~137 vs 100/110 days. FY27 margin targets (9%+, 'closer to 10%') were re-dated to FY28 and then FY29 without acknowledgement; FY27 revenue cut 12-15% -> 8-10% in Nov-26. Under-promised and beat on SAE, cables and T&D share. Misses are usually explained in the next opening remarks (water payments, labour, Middle East war, ROW), but targets are re-set silently. Research, not advice.

data.mcs_scale_note: -1.5 (all moved/dropped) .. +1 (all delivered); weights = specificity(3/2/1) x materiality(1-3) x recency decay (half-life 8 qtrs)
data.grade: D+ (weak credibility on group-level guidance in FY26-27; segment and date promises poor; candour above Skipper because misses are explained in opening remarks)

title: KPIL - Management Credibility Score (T&D peer calibration, Nov 2026)
body: Promise tracker on Kalpataru Projects International (peer calibration for SKIPPER). 7 concalls (Feb-2025 to Aug-2026) plus the Nov-2026 results deck; 78 promises extracted, 63 scored. Status counts: {'delivered': 39, 'unverifiable': 7, 'missed': 11, 'partly': 9, 'moved-goalpost': 1, 'withdrawn': 3, 'pending': 8}. Weighted delivery ratio 76.7% (specificity-only 69.2%; raw hit rate 61.9%); MCS 0.628. Candour index 8.3%. Group-level guidance was met or beaten: FY25 revenue inside the cut 12-13%/13-15% ranges; FY26 revenue +22-23% vs 20%+; consol PBT 4.9% vs 4.5-4.75%; NWC 90 days vs <100; finance cost 1.6% vs <2%; order inflow >26,000 vs 26,000-28,000. Shortfalls: the mid-year raise to '25%+' revenue (delivered 22-23%, later recalled as '20-25%'); Fasttel break-even (ended in a INR 515 cr write-off); asset-sale and collection dates (VEPL two quarters late vs first date; Indore; JJM receivables); capex overspent every guide (~900 vs 600-650). Standalone PBT target met only on the company's adjusted basis (5.9% vs 4.9% reported). Order-inflow guidance was quietly restated downward once (26-28k -> 25k+) before being met. Research, not advice.

title: Base rate for management promise delivery in Indian power T&D / EPC (Skipper vs KEC vs KPIL, Nov 2026)
body: Same-method promise scores for three power T&D / EPC companies (Nov-2026): KPIL 76.7% weighted delivery, SKIPPER 41.3%, KEC 19.8%; peer median 41.3%. Skipper's ~41% is therefore mid-pack, not low: about 7 points below the mean of the other two and slightly below on a sector-adjusted basis (-2.6 pts; KEC -30.3, KPIL 28.8). Sector-wide patterns: (1) FY26 domestic T&D order inflow fell short at all three (Skipper 87-95% of guide, citing CEA holding back bids, ROW and transformer shortages; KPIL India T&D ~7,000 -> 4,500 cr as awards slipped; KEC India T&D ~-11% vs +20% guided, worsened by a company-specific 15-month gap in PGCIL awards after a bribery inquiry raised by analysts); group-level inflow misses were partial (84-100%), not collapses. (2) Dates slip 1-2 quarters everywhere (capacity, plants, asset sales, receivable recoveries). (3) JJM water receivables broke every recovery promise made at KEC and KPIL. (4) Capex/commissioning is the weakest category for the sector (median ~36%). Company-specific: margins, debt and NWC (KEC near zero, KPIL ~100%), and group revenue (16% vs 80%). Volunteered opening-remark guidance delivered far better than Q&A numbers at KEC (48% vs 22%) and KPIL (91% vs 58%) but not at Skipper (39% vs 42%). Use: judge a T&D company's credibility relative to this peer table by category; a raw delivery ratio without a base rate misleads. n=3, so treat as provisional. Research, not advice.

data.metric_definition: SAC = sum over categories c of (n_c / N) x (company delivery% in c - median delivery% in c of the OTHER peers); delivery% = specificity-weighted credit (delivered 1, partly 0.5). Positive = more credible than peers on the same kinds of promise.
data.skipper_sensitivity: Scoring Skipper's FY25 finance-cost miss (4.63% vs <4.5%) as partly under the ceiling rule moves its weighted delivery from 41.3% to 42.2%.
data.caveats: Three companies only; windows differ (Skipper Jul-24 to Oct-26, 10 calls; KEC Feb-25 to Nov-26, 8 calls; KPIL Feb-25 to Aug-26, 7 calls + Nov-26 deck). Skipper was read in full; KEC/KPIL read as full opening remarks + keyword-filtered management answers, so vague promises may be under-counted for the peers.
